title: The client that waits forever on a silent server
summary: A steady_timer puts a deadline on Boost.Asio's async_read_some. Pushing the deadline back calls the old wait with operation_aborted.

turns.user: if the server goes quiet halfway, async_read_some never comes back. drop it after 10s of nothing

assistant.body: Let's give the read a deadline with steady_timer. Asio socket operations take no timeout of their own, so the usual pattern is to close the socket when the timer fires, which ends the pending read with operation_aborted. Every do_read pushes the deadline 10 seconds out with expires_after.

turns.user: first message comes through, then it drops right after. every time. the second read returns operation_aborted

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was incorrect. The timer handler was the cause. When expires_after resets the deadline, the old async_wait is cancelled and its handler still runs, with operation_aborted. Mine closed the socket without looking at ec, so every extension closed the connection. A cancelled wait now does nothing.

sed -i '' 's/async_wait(\[self\](boost::system::error_code) {/async_wait([self](boost::system::error_code ec) {/; s/^      self->socket_\.close();/      if (ec != boost::asio::error::operation_aborted) self->socket_.close();/' src/net/client.cpp

turns.user: fixed. also when the server hangs up first the Client destructor runs 10s late. why

assistant.body: Good catch. After the read ends with eof, the async_wait handler still holds self, so Client lives until the timer fires. When the read fails, cancel the timer too, and the last shared_ptr goes with it.
